text:
Morgan: Quick sync — postmortem follow-ups from Friday's outage. Main takeaway: noisy pages from the backend CPU and the frontend 5xx spike. We promised concrete owners + timelines for dedupe/thresholds/paging policy. Who can own which action items?
Alex: I can take the dedupe logic and rule tuning for backend CPU alerts. Plan: make dedupe key incorporate trace_id + service, bump dedupe window to 10m, and add a cool-down for repetitive flaps. Will post PR by EOD Tue. :+1:
Lee: I will audit the alert rules and current thresholds. I saw a bunch of 85% CPU alerts during GC — we should avoid paging for transient GC blips. Proposing: change paging threshold to 95% sustained for 3m, but keep detector-level metrics for dashboards. Will validate with historical 90d traces.
Jiayi: I'll own paging policy doc updates and the runbook adjustments for oncall. Add a decision for when to escalate to infra vs runtime. Target: publish updated playbook + oncall flow by next Thursday.
Stella: I'll set up a recurring 'noise sweep' 30m weekly for the next 6 weeks to catch regressions and false positives. Will add a calendar invite and a short checklist.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0319 linked to thread, postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-2026-0319 (private).
Morgan: Nice. Let's capture action items here so SRE leads can follow up. I'll list them and owners: 
- AI-1: Deduplicate backend CPU alerts (owner: Alex) — PR + test by 2026-04-07
- AI-2: Threshold audit and historical validation (owner: Lee) — report by 2026-04-05
- AI-3: Update paging/runbook (owner: Jiayi) — doc + diagrams by 2026-04-09
- AI-4: Weekly noise sweeps + checklist (owner: Stella) — recurring event created today
Morgan: Also we saw a recurring pattern: periodic cache regen causes bursts of 5xx on frontend between 02:00-02:20 UTC across 3/7 incidents. We should consider staggered cache warmups or circuit-breaker backoff. Any objections?
Alex: No objections. For cache regen, I'll add jitter to the warmup job and throttle parallelism to 2. Quick snippet I want to try: 
```json
{
  "warmup_parallelism": 2,
  "jitter_seconds": "rand(0,300)"
}
```
Lee: For dedupe specifics: propose dedupe key = "service:cluster:trace_id||request_id" and window 10m. Also add a suppression rule: if same signature fires >5 times in 30m, convert subsequent alerts to internal-only (no page) for 1h.
Jiayi: That suppression idea is good. We'll need product approval if we suppress anything user-facing, but for internal infra pages it's fine. I'll add an approval step in the doc.
Stella: I'll centralize metrics for the sweeps in a dashboard template: queries for 'pages / hour', 'unique signatures', 'avg time to resolve'. Will share template by tomorrow.
Morgan: Can each owner please drop a short note in this thread when their task is complete? Also add the AI IDs to the postmortem checklist.
Alex: Ack — will post PR link here when ready.
Lee: Already started the historical run. ETA 48h.
Jiayi: Doc skeleton up, putting in review.
Stella: Calendar invite sent: "Noise Sweep (eng-oncall)" weekly Weds 09:00 UTC.
oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation change picks up new schedule next Monday.
Morgan: One last ask — keep any new alert rules scoped to team-owned channels and specify SLO/MTTR expectations in the rule metadata. We don't want untriaged alert ownership.
Alex: Agreed. I'll add metadata block to the PR: team, owner, SLO, runbook_link.
Lee: Can we also add a small smoke test that simulates a GC spike so we can verify no pages? I can add a K6 script to our infra-test repo.
Jiayi: Good call. Add the test link to the runbook so oncall can run it if they suspect noisy pages.
Morgan: Perfect. Thanks all — we'll reconvene after the PRs/docs land. :rocket:
